title: GEO vs SEO vs AEO: Differences Explained (2026)
excerpt: GEO vs SEO vs AEO explained: definitions, what SEO for AI is called, a comparison table, which to prioritize, a combined checklist and how to measure each.
keywords: what is seo for ai called
aeo and geo in digital marketing
author: AI Brand Track Team
content:
SEO (search engine optimization) gets your pages ranked and clicked in Google and Bing. GEO (generative engine optimization) gets your brand mentioned and cited inside AI-generated answers from ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, Claude and Google AI Overviews. AEO (answer engine optimization) gets your content picked as *the* direct answer to a question, whether that is a featured snippet, a voice assistant reply or an AI answer. They overlap heavily: in our experience AEO and GEO are often used interchangeably, and good SEO is the foundation that both depend on.

## SEO, GEO and AEO defined

- **SEO** is the established discipline of making a website crawlable, relevant and authoritative so it ranks in search results. The output is a ranked list of links, and success means the user clicks through to your site.
- **GEO** focuses on generative AI tools that write an answer instead of listing links. The goal is for your brand to be named, recommended, described accurately and ideally cited as a source when someone asks a question in your category.
- **AEO** covers featured snippets, "People Also Ask" boxes and voice assistants, where one answer is read out or shown above the results. The term is now also applied to AI answers, which is why it collides with GEO.

Our point of view: these are not three separate strategies. They are three lenses on one job, which is being the most useful, trustworthy and easy-to-quote source on your topic. You'll find articles that draw sharp lines between AEO and GEO; others, like Profound, argue in [their own write-up](https://www.tryprofound.com/blog/aeo-vs-geo) that AEO and GEO are effectively the same thing. We think the difference is mostly emphasis and which metric you watch.

## What is SEO for AI called?

There is no single official name yet. You will see all of these used for roughly the same work:

| Name | Stands for | Where you'll see it |
|---|---|---|
| **GEO** | Generative engine optimization | A common term in marketing content and tooling; also the title of a [2023 research paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.09735) by a team including Princeton researchers (presented at KDD 2024) that we think helped popularize it |
| **AEO** | Answer engine optimization | In our experience, popular with SEO platforms and agencies, especially when featured snippets and voice are included |
| **AIO** | AI optimization (sometimes "AI Overviews optimization") | Less common; can be confusing because it also refers to Google AI Overviews |
| **LLMO / LLM SEO** | Large language model optimization | Used when the focus is how models understand and describe your brand as an entity |
| **AI SEO** | AI search engine optimization | Broad and ambiguous: can also mean using AI tools to do SEO |
| **Search everywhere optimization** | Optimizing for every place people search | Used by some educators, such as the [Digital Marketing Institute](https://digitalmarketinginstitute.com/blog/what-is-seo-geo-and-aeo), as an umbrella term for SEO, GEO and AEO done together |

If you need one term, in our experience **GEO** and **AEO** are the two you'll hear most, and they're frequently paired as "AEO and GEO." You could also skip the new acronyms and just call it SEO, which is fair: most of the work is good SEO done with AI answers in mind. For a deeper look at each label, see our guides to [generative engine optimization](/generative-engine-optimization), [answer engine optimization](/answer-engine-optimization) and [LLM SEO](/llm-seo).

## SEO vs GEO vs AEO: comparison table

| | SEO | GEO | AEO |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Goal** | Rank pages high and win clicks | Get your brand mentioned, recommended and cited in generated answers | Be selected as the single direct answer to a question |
| **Where you appear** | Google and Bing organic results | ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, Claude, Google AI Overviews and AI Mode | Featured snippets, People Also Ask, voice assistants, AI answers |
| **What success looks like** | Top-3 positions, organic traffic, conversions | Your brand named (ideally first) and described accurately, your URLs cited | Your wording or page shown as the answer, often without a click |
| **Main tactics** | Keyword targeting, technical health, internal links, backlinks | Quotable passages, entity consistency, third-party mentions, crawlable pages for AI bots | Question-led headings, short direct answers, lists and tables, FAQ and schema markup |
| **How to measure** | Rankings, impressions, clicks, organic sessions | Mention rate, share of voice, position in answer, sentiment, citations | Snippet ownership, PAA presence, appearance in AI answers for target questions |
| **Typical tools** | Search Console, rank trackers, crawlers, keyword tools | AI visibility trackers, manual prompt testing, citation analysis | Rank trackers with SERP-feature tracking, schema validators, AI visibility trackers |

A page built for AEO (clear question, concise answer) is also the kind of passage a generative engine likes to lift, and both rely on that page being indexed and trusted, which is SEO.

## GEO vs SEO

The core difference is **the format of the result**. SEO competes for a position in a list of ten links. GEO competes for a mention inside a paragraph the AI writes, where only a handful of brands get named. Two practical differences follow:

1. **The unit of success.** In SEO it's a page ranking for a keyword. In GEO it's your *brand* appearing in an answer, often for a conversational prompt like "What's the best accounting software for a freelance designer?" that no one would type into Google word for word.
2. **Who shapes the result.** SEO is mostly about your own pages plus the links pointing to them. GEO leans heavily on what *other* sites say about you: review platforms, "best X" roundups, forums, news and comparison articles. Models build their picture of your brand from all of it: [OpenAI, for example, says](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/7842364-how-chatgpt-and-our-foundation-models-are-developed) its models are developed partly from information publicly available on the internet.

What stays the same: AI tools that search the web retrieve pages from search indexes. [ChatGPT search sometimes partners with other search providers](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/9237897-searching-the-web-with-chatgpt), [PerplexityBot](https://docs.perplexity.ai/guides/bots) exists to surface and link sites in Perplexity's search results, and [Google's AI features](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/ai-features) only link to pages that are indexed in Google Search. If your page can't be crawled or doesn't rank, it's much less likely to be retrieved and cited. That's why GEO doesn't replace SEO; it sits on top of it. Our [AI search engine optimization playbook](/blog/ai-search-engine-optimization) covers the full GEO checklist, including AI crawler access in robots.txt.

## AEO vs SEO

AEO is the narrowest of the three. SEO asks "how do I rank for this topic?" AEO asks "how do I become the answer to this exact question?"

AEO in practice:

- Writing headings as real questions ("How much does a home energy audit cost?")
- Answering in the first 1-3 sentences under each heading, before the detail
- Using formats that are easy to extract: definitions, numbered steps, short tables
- Adding `FAQPage`, `HowTo` or `Product` structured data where it genuinely fits
- Covering the follow-up questions that appear in People Also Ask

A classic AEO win: someone asks a voice assistant "how long should I boil an egg," and the assistant reads your sentence aloud. In our experience, the same structure also helps in AI Overviews and chat answers, which is why AEO and GEO blur together.

The trade-off is clicks: when you *are* the answer, some users never visit your page. [Pew Research found](https://www.pewresearch.org/short-reads/2025/07/22/google-users-are-less-likely-to-click-on-links-when-an-ai-summary-appears-in-the-results/) that Google users were less likely to click on links when an AI summary appeared in the results. AEO pays off most for brand exposure and questions where the answer leads to a next step on your site.

## AEO vs GEO: the difference explained with examples

If you want to separate them, the cleanest distinction is this: **AEO targets one extracted answer; GEO targets inclusion in a synthesized answer.**

**AEO example.** A user searches Google for "what is a 529 plan." A featured snippet shows a two-sentence definition taken from one page. The page that wrote the clearest, most direct definition wins that box. One source, one answer, usually a direct quote.

**GEO example.** A user asks ChatGPT or Perplexity, "Which 529 plans have the lowest fees for out-of-state residents?" The AI pulls from several pages, combines them into a new answer, names three or four plans and links a few sources. There is no single "winning" page. Success means your brand is among those named, described correctly and ideally cited.

| | AEO | GEO |
|---|---|---|
| **Answer type** | Extracted (lifted from one source) | Generated (synthesized from many sources) |
| **Typical query** | Short factual question | Conversational, comparative or recommendation prompt |
| **Win condition** | Your text is the answer | Your brand is in the answer |
| **Biggest lever** | Page structure and concise answers | Off-site reputation and entity consistency, plus quotable pages |

In everyday use, though, both labels get applied to the same tactics. Ask an agency or tool what they actually measure rather than debating the label.

## Where SEO, GEO and AEO overlap

Think of a three-circle Venn diagram.

**All three (the center):**
- Crawlable, fast, server-rendered pages
- Helpful content written by people who know the subject
- Clear site structure and internal linking
- Authority built through mentions and links from reputable sites
- Accurate, up-to-date facts (pricing, features, locations)

**AEO + GEO:**
- Answer-first writing and question-led headings
- Tables, lists and definitions that are easy to extract
- Structured data that makes facts unambiguous

**SEO + GEO:**
- Ranking in the indexes AI tools retrieve from
- Earning coverage on sites that rank for "best X" queries

**Mostly GEO only:**
- Consistent brand description across every profile and directory
- Presence in reviews, forums and community discussions
- Monitoring how models describe your brand and fixing inaccuracies at the source

**Mostly SEO only:** title tags, click-through optimization and keyword-level rank tracking.

## Which should you prioritize first?

Start from your situation, not the acronym.

- **New site with little traffic:** SEO fundamentals first. Without indexed, crawlable, decent-ranking pages, neither answer boxes nor AI tools have much to retrieve.
- **Established site with good rankings:** Add AEO formatting to your top pages, then check where you stand in AI answers. You may be ranking well on Google and still be missing from ChatGPT's recommendations.
- **B2B or SaaS in a competitive category:** Prioritize GEO. Buyers can ask AI tools for shortlists and comparisons, and in our experience those answers often lean on third-party reviews and roundups. Invest in comparison pages, review profiles and earned coverage.
- **Local business:** Classic local SEO (Google Business Profile, reviews, accurate listings) still does most of the heavy lifting, and we'd expect those same signals to inform AI answers about local providers.

## A combined SEO, AEO and GEO checklist

One list, ordered roughly from foundation to compounding work:

1. **Make sure you can be crawled.** Allow search and AI search bots (such as `OAI-SearchBot`, `PerplexityBot`, `Claude-SearchBot`, documented by [OpenAI](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/bots), [Perplexity](https://docs.perplexity.ai/guides/bots) and [Anthropic](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/8896518-does-anthropic-crawl-data-from-the-web-and-how-can-site-owners-block-the-crawler)) in robots.txt and your firewall, and serve key content in the HTML.
2. **Fix technical SEO basics.** Indexing, canonical tags, page speed, internal links.
3. **Map the questions buyers ask.** List 20-50 real questions and prompts, for example:

```
What is the best [category] for [use case]?
[Your brand] vs [competitor]: which is better?
Alternatives to [competitor] for small teams
How much does [category] cost?
Is [your brand] worth it?
```

4. **Answer each one on a clear page.** Question-style heading, direct answer in the first sentences, then detail, examples and a table where it helps.
5. **Add structured data** that matches visible content: `Organization` with `sameAs`, `Product` or `SoftwareApplication`, `FAQPage` where you have real Q&A.
6. **Make your entity consistent.** Same name, category and one-line description on your site, LinkedIn, review platforms and directories.
7. **Earn third-party mentions.** Reviews, "best X" roundups, podcasts, guest articles, honest community participation. Check which sources AI tools cite for your prompts and target those.
8. **Publish something original.** Data, benchmarks or firm opinions give both search engines and AI tools a reason to cite you specifically.
9. **Keep facts fresh.** Update pricing, features and comparisons, and show a visible "last updated" date.
10. **Measure all three** on a regular schedule (next section).

## How to measure SEO, AEO and GEO

**SEO** is the easiest: Search Console for impressions, clicks and queries; a rank tracker for positions; analytics for organic sessions and conversions.

**AEO** adds SERP features. Rank trackers with SERP-feature tracking can report whether you own the featured snippet or appear in People Also Ask for a keyword. Track that for your target questions. For Google's own AI answers, Search Console now has a [generative AI performance report](https://support.google.com/webmasters/answer/16984139) that shows impressions from AI Overviews and AI Mode by page, country, device and date. It reports impressions only, not clicks or queries.

**GEO** needs a different approach, because there is no "position 3" in a chat answer. Track:

- **Mention rate:** share of your test prompts where your brand appears
- **Share of voice:** your mentions versus competitors across the same prompts
- **Position in the answer:** named first, mid-list or as an afterthought
- **Sentiment and accuracy:** is the description correct and favorable?
- **Citations:** which URLs (yours and third parties') get cited as sources
- **Platform split:** ChatGPT vs Perplexity vs Gemini vs Claude

Because AI answers can vary per run, model version and location (in our experience they often do), and ChatGPT can also draw on [saved memories and past chats](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/8590148-memory-in-chatgpt), run each prompt several times and look at trends rather than single screenshots. You can do this manually with a spreadsheet (prompt, platform, date, mentioned y/n, position, competitors named, sources cited), but it gets tedious quickly, and Google Alerts and classic rank trackers aren't built to monitor AI answers.

An [AI rank tracker](/ai-rank-tracker) automates the GEO side. AI Brand Track, for example, takes your website URL, identifies your brand, industry and competitors, queries ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity and Gemini with industry prompts, and returns a 0-100 visibility score, competitor rankings, sentiment and share of voice in about a minute. Other AI visibility tools exist too; whatever you use, keep your prompt set consistent so results stay comparable. For the full process, see [how to track brand visibility in AI platforms](/blog/how-to-track-brand-visibility-in-ai-platforms).

## Common myths

**"SEO is dead."** It isn't. AI search tools retrieve from the web ([ChatGPT search, for example, sometimes partners with search providers](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/9237897-searching-the-web-with-chatgpt)), and Google's AI Overviews draw on Google's own index. [Google's guidance on AI features](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/ai-features) says a page only needs to be indexed and eligible for a snippet, and that normal SEO best practices still apply. What's changed is that rankings alone no longer show the whole picture.

**"GEO replaces SEO."** GEO extends SEO. Strip away crawlability, quality content and authority, and there is very little left for a generative engine to cite.

**"You need separate teams for SEO, AEO and GEO."** Most of the work is shared. In our view, one team with a combined checklist and one extra measurement layer for AI answers is usually enough.

## FAQ

### What is the difference between GEO, SEO and AEO?

SEO aims to rank your pages in search results and earn clicks. AEO aims to make your content the direct answer to a specific question, as in featured snippets and voice results. GEO aims to get your brand mentioned and cited in answers generated by AI tools like ChatGPT and Perplexity. SEO underpins the other two.

### Is AI SEO the same as GEO?

Mostly, yes. In our experience, "AI SEO" is often used as a synonym for GEO, AEO or LLM optimization, meaning work that improves how AI tools mention your brand. But "AI SEO" can also mean using AI tools to do traditional SEO. GEO is the more specific term for optimizing for generative AI answers.

### What does AEO stand for?

AEO stands for answer engine optimization. It means structuring content so search engines, voice assistants and AI tools pick it as the direct answer to a question.

### Will AEO replace SEO?

No. AEO depends on SEO, because a page generally has to be indexed and trusted before it can be chosen as an answer ([Google's AI features](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/ai-features), for example, require a page to be indexed and eligible for a snippet). What's changing is the emphasis: when a search ends in a direct answer, being that answer matters. Treat AEO as a layer on top of SEO, not a replacement.

### Is GEO better than SEO?

Neither is better; they measure different outcomes. SEO drives clicks from search results, while GEO shapes whether AI tools recommend your brand when buyers ask for options. In our view, most businesses need both, and strong SEO makes GEO easier because AI tools that search the web draw on search indexes ([Google's AI features](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/ai-features), for example, only link to indexed pages).

### Is SEO dead or evolving in 2026?

SEO is evolving. Crawlable pages, useful content and authority still decide what search engines and AI tools can find and trust. The change is in what you measure and how you write: answer-first content, consistent brand information across the web, and tracking AI mentions alongside rankings.

### How do you use AEO and GEO together?

Use AEO tactics to make each page easy to quote (question headings, direct answers, tables, schema), and GEO tactics to make your brand widely and consistently described off-site (reviews, roundups, community discussions). Then measure both: snippet and answer ownership for AEO, and mention rate, share of voice and citations across ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini and Claude for GEO.
